name: Binance

summary.text: Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, founded by Changpeng Zhao. On November 21, 2023 the company pleaded guilty to U.S. federal charges including Bank Secrecy Act violations and agreed to pay about $4.3 billion to the Justice Department, Treasury's FinCEN and OFAC and the CFTC; Zhao pleaded guilty, resigned as chief executive and was succeeded by Richard Teng. In March 2025 Abu Dhabi's MGX took a minority stake for $2 billion, Binance's first institutional investment, settled in a stablecoin later identified as World Liberty Financial's USD1. In October 2025 President Trump pardoned Zhao; Senate Democrats then wrote to the Justice Department and Treasury about the pardon and the USD1 relationship.

facts.claim: On November 21, 2023, Binance agreed to pay $4.3 billion to the U.S. Justice Department, the Treasury Department, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Office of Foreign Assets Control to resolve charges covering Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions violations and failure to register as a money transmitting business. Attorney General Merrick Garland said Binance became the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange in part because of the crimes it committed.
facts.quote: Binance agreed to pay $4.3 billion to the Justice Department, the Treasury Department, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Office of Foreign Assets Control, covering Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions violations and the failure to register as a money transmitting business.

sources.title: Binance CEO steps down; crypto platform hit with record $4.3 billion in damages
Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao pleads guilty to federal charges, steps down

facts.claim: As part of the November 2023 resolution, founder Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty in Seattle federal court to failing to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, agreed to a $50 million personal fine and stepped down as chief executive; Richard Teng, the company's global head of regional markets, was named CEO.
facts.quote: Richard Teng, the company's former global head of regional markets, was named the new CEO of Binance.

sources.title: Binance names new CEO after taking $4.3B in penalties
Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao pleads guilty to federal charges, steps down

facts.claim: On March 12, 2025, Binance announced that Abu Dhabi-based MGX had acquired a minority stake for $2 billion, described by Binance as the first institutional investment in the exchange and by the companies as MGX's first entry into crypto and blockchain; the investment was paid in a stablecoin not named at the time.
facts.quote: Binance said Abu Dhabi's MGX has acquired a minority stake for $2 billion, the first institutional investment in the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

sources.title: Binance secures $2 billion investment from Abu Dhabi's MGX in landmark crypto deal
Binance Says Abu Dhabi's MGX Makes $2 Billion Investment

facts.claim: In May 2025 Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley wrote to the chief executives of MGX and Binance requesting documents on the use of World Liberty Financial's USD1 stablecoin to settle MGX's $2 billion investment in Binance. The letter is a request for records, not a finding.
facts.quote: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley sent a letter to the CEOs of MGX and Binance requesting documents on their use of USD1 to settle the $2 billion investment.

sources.title: Warren, Merkley Seek Records on $2 Billion Trump Stablecoin Deal from UAE Firm and Binance

facts.claim: Binance CEO Richard Teng told CNBC in November 2025 that the use of USD1 for the MGX transaction was decided by MGX, and that USD1 had been listed on other exchanges before Binance added it. The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Binance also assisted in building the technology behind the stablecoin; a Bloomberg report said Binance wrote USD1's foundational smart-contract code, which a Binance spokesperson answered by saying the listing followed its standard process and which Zhao called a 'hit piece'.
facts.quote: CEO Richard Teng told CNBC that the usage of USD1 for the transaction was decided by MGX, and he noted that USD1 had already been listed on other exchanges before Binance added it.

facts.claim: Binance added USD1 trading pairs after the MGX investment, which The Block described as elevating the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial stablecoin.
facts.quote: Binance elevates Trump-backed World Liberty's stablecoin by adding USD1 trading pairs

sources.title: Binance elevates Trump-backed World Liberty's stablecoin by adding USD1 trading pairs

facts.claim: On October 28, 2025, Senate Banking Committee Democrats wrote to the Justice Department and the Treasury about President Trump's October 23, 2025 pardon of Zhao, noting that Zhao had personally paid a $50 million fine and served nearly four months in prison after pleading guilty to the anti-money-laundering charge. The letter is a congressional inquiry.
facts.quote: On October 23, 2025, President Trump granted that pardon.

connections.claim: MGX, the Abu Dhabi investment firm formed by Mubadala and G42, took a minority stake in Binance for $2 billion, announced March 12, 2025, paid in stablecoin.
connections.quote: MGX, a joint venture between sovereign wealth fund Mubadala and AI firm G42, aims to leverage this partnership to drive innovation at the intersection of AI, blockchain, and decentralized finance (DeFi).

sources.title: Binance secures $2 billion investment from Abu Dhabi's MGX in landmark crypto deal

connections.claim: MGX's $2 billion investment in Binance was settled in World Liberty Financial's USD1 stablecoin, and Binance subsequently listed USD1 trading pairs; Binance says MGX chose the stablecoin, while the Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reported Binance helped build USD1's technology, which Binance and Zhao dispute.
connections.quote: The deal was settled using USD1, a stablecoin created by the Trump family's crypto venture, World Liberty Financial.

openQuestions: The Justice Department's own November 2023 press release and plea documents were not returned by the search; the court items rely on CNBC, NBC and Banking Dive accounts of the plea and resolution.
The size of MGX's stake in Binance was not disclosed in the sources reached.
The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reports on Binance's role in building USD1 were reached only through secondary coverage; the originals should be checked.
The date on which Binance listed USD1 was not confirmed.
